title: U.S. House · North Carolina's 2nd District

context.text: Both the Democratic and Republican primaries for this seat were canceled, with Deborah Ross and Eugene Douglass advancing unopposed. Incumbent Deborah Ross (D) faces Eugene Douglass (R) and Matthew Laszacs (L) in the general election.

candidates.name: Deborah Ross

summary.text: Deborah Ross is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in North Carolina's 2nd Congressional District, which includes most of Wake County. A civil rights and clean energy attorney, she served in the North Carolina House from 2003 to 2013, was the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2016, and has represented the district in Congress since 2021. She serves on the House Judiciary, Ethics, and Science, Space, and Technology committees.

background.text: Born in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, in 1963. According to her official House biography, she grew up in a small town as the daughter of an Air Force veteran and an early childhood education teacher.
Earned a bachelor's degree in international relations from Brown University in 1985 and a law degree from the University of North Carolina Law School in 1990.

Worked as a civil rights lawyer before holding public office; her official biography says she helped pass the South's first anti-racial profiling law and reforms to the state's juvenile justice laws. She later worked in private practice on North Carolina's clean energy sector.

Won a seat representing Wake County in the North Carolina House of Representatives in 2002 and served from 2003 to 2013 (District 34), including on the Education, Elections, Ethics, Finance and Judiciary committees.
Was the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2016, losing the general election to incumbent Republican Richard Burr.
Won the open 2nd Congressional District seat in the November 2020 general election, succeeding Republican George E.B. Holding, and has been re-elected in 2022 and 2024.

In the 119th Congress (2025-2026), serves on the House Judiciary Committee, the Ethics Committee, and the Science, Space, and Technology Committee, and is a Chief Deputy Whip and a member of the Steering and Policy Committee for House Democrats.

Her official biography states that 17 pieces of her legislation have been signed into law, including bills on funding for sexual assault nurse examiners, accountability for perpetrators of child sexual abuse, judicial ethics and transparency, and North Carolina's offshore wind energy potential.

priorities.text: Building an economy that gives every American a real shot, including policies to create jobs, lower costs, and spur innovation.
Lowering health care costs, citing work on the Inflation Reduction Act's insulin cap and Medicare drug price negotiation and her earlier push to expand Medicaid in North Carolina.
Expanding North Carolina's clean energy economy, including legislation on offshore wind leasing and electric vehicle adoption.

positions.summary: Says she has worked for decades to protect access to abortion and contraception and wants Roe v. Wade codified into federal law.
positions.quote: Since the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade, I've been fighting in Congress against extreme Republican attacks on women's fundamental right to make decisions about our own bodies. I will not stop until Roe v. Wade is codified into federal law and every single woman – no matter her zip code – has full access to reproductive care.

positions.summary: Cites her work on the Inflation Reduction Act's health provisions and, as a state legislator, pushing to expand Medicaid in North Carolina.
positions.quote: As a state legislator for more than a decade, I worked with my colleagues to expand Medicaid in North Carolina. I'm grateful that North Carolina became the 40th state to finally vote to expand Medicaid in 2023.

positions.summary: Highlights legislation she sponsored to overturn a moratorium on offshore wind leasing and expand electric vehicle adoption, framing clean energy investment as central to fighting climate change.
positions.quote: Investing in clean energy technology is one of the best resources in our toolbox to combat climate change – now and for future generations.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary (Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet Subcommittee; Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement Subcommittee), the Committee on Ethics, and the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Energy and Environment subcommittees).
Introduced the bipartisan America's CHILDREN Act, which would protect children of long-term visa holders ("Documented Dreamers") from aging out of the immigration system at age 21.

Sponsored legislation to overturn the 10-year moratorium on offshore wind leasing off North Carolina and other Southeastern states, enacted as part of the Inflation Reduction Act; also sponsored a bill to encourage electric vehicle development and adoption, enacted as part of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.

candidates.name: Eugene Douglass
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Republican primary.

summary.text: Eugene (Gene) Douglass is the Republican nominee challenging incumbent Deborah Ross in North Carolina's 2nd Congressional District. He describes himself as a retired chemistry professor and has run for federal office in Hawaii, New Hampshire, and, in the 2024 Republican primary, North Carolina's 2nd District.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from The King's College in 1979 (chemistry and math, according to his questionnaire), a graduate degree from the University of Connecticut in 1982, and a Ph.D. in fiber and polymer science from North Carolina State University in 2010; also graduated from Bethel Theological Seminary in San Diego.

In a 2024 News & Observer candidate questionnaire, listed his professional experience as a college/university chemistry professor and his current occupation as consultant; his campaign newsletter describes him as a retired chemistry professor. Ballotpedia lists his professional experience as scientist and notes an affiliation with the American Chemistry Society.
According to his 2024 questionnaire, ran for U.S. Senate in Hawaii in 1998 and 2000 and for New Hampshire's 2nd Congressional District in 2002.
Ran in the March 5, 2024 Republican primary for North Carolina's 2nd Congressional District; Alan Swain won the nomination.
Became the Republican nominee for the district in 2026.

priorities.text: A smaller federal government, less regulation and lower taxes, with responsibility returned to the states.
Eliminating the federal Department of Education and returning education policy to state and local authorities.
Opposing abortion, saying he wants to protect human life from conception until natural death.

positions.summary: Says he wants to protect human life from conception until natural death and end abortion used for birth control, with states regulating the procedure.
Lists lower taxes and a smaller federal government among his top three campaign messages.

candidates.researchNotes: Douglass has not previously held elected office; positions are drawn from his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey. No campaign website was located.

candidates.name: Matthew Laszacs
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from a canceled Libertarian Party primary.

summary.text: Matthew Laszacs is the Libertarian Party nominee in North Carolina's 2nd Congressional District. He describes himself as a business executive with 20 years of experience, and has previously appeared on North Carolina state legislative general-election ballots. He says Congress has ceded too much power to the executive and judicial branches.

background.text: According to his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey, was born in Philadelphia, the son of military parents, and raised in Millington, Tennessee; he moved to North Carolina in 2001 and has lived there since.
Earned a bachelor's degree in business administration from North Carolina Wesleyan College (2009) while working full time and raising two children.
Describes himself as a business executive with 20 years of experience building and leading teams.

Ballotpedia lists campaign finance records for him in two prior general elections: North Carolina State Senate District 14 (2022) and North Carolina House of Representatives District 41 (2024), both of which he lost.
Advanced to the 2026 general election after the March 3, 2026 Libertarian primary for the district was canceled.

priorities.text: Restoring Congress's Article I powers to check the executive branch and rein in the judiciary.
Addressing federal fiscal problems, including debt, inflation, and the approaching Social Security budget crisis.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions are drawn from Laszacs' 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey; no campaign website content beyond the survey was reviewed within the research budget.
